paper_core_claims.claim: Church is a dynamically typed applicative-order stochastic Lisp in which pure Lisp is deterministic, elementary random procedures introduce sampling, first-class expressions compose generative processes, eval samples them and query denotes conditional sampling.

Admissible expressions, including expressions with stochastic memoization, induce probability distributions over equivalence classes of evaluation histories and hence return values; positive-probability predicates give well-defined conditional query distributions.
Stochastic mem shares sampled generative history across calls, provides persistent random-world structure and can express Dirichlet-process memoization and several nonparametric models compactly.
Exact rejection and collapsed rejection implement query in principle, while a Metropolis-Hastings algorithm over computation traces is proposed for approximate conditional inference.

A single higher-order language can express causal Bayes-style models, infinite mixture/relational models, stochastic transition grammars and planning by inference without model-specific inference code.

function_concept_used_by_paper: A Church expression is a first-class higher-order stochastic function/program describing a generative process. Ordinary procedures close over an environment; elementary random procedures additionally expose a conditional probability function; eval turns expressions into samples; query conditions their induced history/value distribution; mem converts an admissible procedure into a persistent random function; and nested eval/query lets programs manipulate or reason about programs.
representation_or_carrier: Syntax and Scheme-like values are countable; real numbers are fixed/floating approximations. A procedure is body, arguments and environment, with elementary random procedures adding a distribution function. The semantic carrier is an evaluation history and its product probability; admissible expressions have total finite-history weight one and induce a value distribution mu(e,env). With mem, histories are quotiented by unused memo-table values. Approximate runtime state is a computation-trace DAG containing an evaluation tree, environment-extension tree and binding dependencies.
specification_language: Church provides dynamically typed Lisp syntax for constants, variables, application, lambda, if, define and quote; a standard library supplies higher-order operations and elementary random procedures; eval/query/lex-query specify generative and conditional computation; mem/DPmem specify persistent and exchangeable random functions. It does not statically specify types, support, admissibility, termination, evidence positivity, resource bounds, inference accuracy, convergence diagnostics, privacy, deployment or lifecycle policy, and the paper gives no machine-checkable contract language.
compiler_or_generator: No compiler or ahead-of-time generator is presented. The paper gives an informal interpreter definition and suggests future program analyses that might transform query into eval for exact enumeration. Because expressions are values, Church can describe priors over programs and program induction, but this is a representational possibility rather than an implemented or verified synthesis compiler.
interpreter_or_runtime: A prototype implements Scheme-like eval, finite memo tables and query. Exact recursive rejection is definable metacircularly but can be nonterminating or intractable; collapsed rejection marginalizes predicate randomness. Approximate query uses Metropolis-Hastings proposals over evaluation-history traces, repairing dependent evaluations and applying proposal corrections. At publication the MCMC implementation omitted mem, did not fully handle nested queries, omitted delicate trace-update equations for space and was explicitly too inefficient for typical machine-learning applications.
composition_rule: Lambda abstraction/application and higher-order functions compose deterministic and stochastic procedures; lexical environments route bindings; eval recursively composes sampling histories; query conditions the composed history distribution; mem shares results by procedure/argument; DPmem composes a Dirichlet-process cache; nested eval/query composes inference and program interpretation. Composition does not ensure admissibility, positive evidence, efficient inference, good mixing or bounded memory.
state_or_effect_model: Random primitive calls are probabilistic effects recorded in evaluation histories. Memoization creates persistent per-argument random state and supports random worlds; query conditions effects; recursion may diverge; approximate inference mutates a trace proposal. The denotational language is intended to preserve exchangeability/purity, while its finite implementation necessarily uses mutable association lists. General mutable state, concurrency, distributed execution, I/O failure, checkpointing and durable provenance are outside scope.
uncertainty_model: Uncertainty is a probability distribution over finite evaluation histories and marginal return values; conditional uncertainty is defined by query when the expression/predicate are admissible and the predicate has positive probability. Memoized random functions share latent variables; DPmem supplies nonparametric uncertainty; approximate MCMC adds algorithmic error. The paper gives no finite-sample error bound, posterior calibration, mixing theorem, ESS, acceptance-rate report, confidence interval or systematic comparison with ground truth.

validation_regime.formal: two lemmas and one theorem with proof sketches establish history weight, admissibility with mem and well-defined positive-evidence conditional queries
validation_regime.implementation: a Blaise-based prototype is said to be implemented and verified on examples exercising recursion/trace updates; mem was not implemented in MCMC and nested-query details were not handled
validation_regime.examples: code listings cover a sprinkler model, infinite mixtures/relational models, PCFG/HDP-HMM/adaptor grammar and a red-light planning model
validation_regime.reported_results: Figure 6 shows qualitative collapsed-rejection posterior samples for two tiny Gaussian-mixture datasets; Figure 7 plots planning action probability for gamma=.2 and cheat-det=.7; Figure 9 shows one sprinkler MCMC run over 100 samples with 30 MCMC steps per query sample
validation_regime.boundary: there are no datasets, released artifact, repeated runs, exact-target comparison, error bars, acceptance/mixing diagnostics, runtime/memory measurements, ablations or benchmarks; formal arguments are proof sketches rather than mechanized proofs

equivalence_notions.boundary: The paper sketches the measure construction and gives no executable equivalence checker.
Syntactically distinct programs can agree distributionally, but no general decision procedure is supplied.
Undefined for inadmissible expressions and requires the conditioning event to have positive probability.
Trace repair details are omitted, nested-query support is incomplete and the MCMC implementation did not yet support mem.
No convergence/mixing proof or quantitative target-agreement experiment is supplied for the proposed MCMC implementation.

lifecycle_and_provenance: The 2008 paper is preserved by the official UAI site and a 2024 PMLR reissue with byte-identical PDFs, plus a separately hash-bound arXiv minor-corrections version. The provisional resolver instead captured an unrelated 2016 textbook homepage; its exact hash is reproducible only over HTTP because the current HTTPS hostname certificate does not validate. The paper cites a Blaise-based prototype and thesis but supplies no source URL, release tag, build instructions, dependency/runtime lock, test corpus, random seeds, trace archive, CI, security policy, compatibility matrix, revalidation cadence, rollback or retirement record. Later Church/WebChurch systems are not evidence that this specific 2008 artifact was reproducible as published.
limitations_and_failure_boundaries: The universal-language claim is about expressive computability/generative description, not guaranteed termination, normalized probability, efficient inference or practical learnability.
Only admissible expressions with total finite-history weight one define value distributions; recursion/fix can be inadmissible, and no admissibility checker is provided.
Query is undefined if the expression or predicate is inadmissible or if no supported value makes the predicate true with non-zero probability.
Recursive rejection query may not terminate for impossible evidence and is expected to be intractable for many low-probability events.
Countable primitive types and fixed/floating representations bound the language's numeric model; continuous distributions are runtime primitives rather than a measure-theoretic language proof here.
Formal semantic results are proof sketches, including the countably infinite memoized environment and quotient over histories; they are not mechanized.
Stochastic memoization can imply infinitely many latent values denotationally; the finite runtime creates entries lazily and can grow without a resource bound.
Exchangeability is proposed as stochastic purity, but general stateful extensions and their semantic conditions are explicitly future work.
The prototype MCMC algorithm had not implemented programs using mem, despite mem being a central language feature.
Nested-query handling is acknowledged as incomplete, and delicate trace-consistency/proposal corrections are omitted from the paper.
The MCMC section gives no stationarity, irreducibility, convergence-rate, mixing, variance or finite-sample correctness theorem.
Figure 9 is one 100-sample sprinkler run with 30 MCMC steps per sample, not a reproducibility or convergence study; no exact target or uncertainty band is shown.
Figures 6-7 are illustrative qualitative outputs with tiny synthetic setups, not empirical validation across tasks or comparison to baselines.
The authors explicitly state that the implementation is not efficient enough for typical machine-learning applications.
No runnable paper artifact, code receipt, seeds, environment, datasets, tests or trace logs accompany the source.
The registered probmods URL is an unrelated textbook landing page and its HTTPS certificate currently fails hostname validation, demonstrating weak source-registry lifecycle hygiene.
The paper does not connect Church semantics to neural weights, governed Function OS assets, ignition epsilon, frozen Psi_0 or production deployment.
what_the_paper_does_not_support: It does not prove that all Church programs terminate, normalize or admit well-defined conditional queries.
It does not provide complete or efficient generic inference for programs using mem, nested queries or rare/impossible evidence.
It does not provide an automatic equivalence checker, compiler, convergence-certified MCMC runtime or current reproducible release.
It does not establish quantitative superiority across Bayesian networks, nonparametric models, grammars or planning tasks.
It does not empirically validate neural function composition, artifact lifecycle governance, a probability law for ignition epsilon or ignition itself.

confirmed_projection: Within the paper's admissible-program and prototype boundaries, Church confirms a stochastic FunctionSpec-Representation-Interpreter-ExecutionTrace-Composer architecture: higher-order expressions denote history/value distributions, query specifies conditioning, mem carries persistent latent state, and exact/approximate inference targets operate over explicit traces. Compiler, executable Artifact, robust Validator and VersionedRegistry closure remain partial.
source_specific_reasoning: CONFIRMED is warranted for the bounded architectural claim because the full primary paper specifies a stochastic higher-order language, gives semantic proof sketches, defines exact conditional query, constructs persistent random functions and describes a trace-based approximate runtime with concrete examples. The status does not endorse the broadest universality rhetoric or production readiness: admissibility and positive evidence are mandatory, inference can be nonterminating/intractable, MCMC omitted mem/nested details, validation is qualitative and no runnable artifact survives in the paper record.
projection_boundary: These are 121CX projections from the complete byte-identical official UAI/PMLR 10-page paper, the full arXiv minor-corrections version, all rendered pages, official PMLR metadata and the exact registered-but-unrelated probmods HTML.
